description: Pasco, WA photography by Lisa Weiss: golden-hour family and senior portraits, in-home newborn sessions, branding photography and professional headshots.

hero.heading: Pasco, WA Photographer
hero.intro: Family sessions and senior pictures in Pasco's open evening light, plus in-home newborn photography, branding sessions and professional headshots — where the sky feels wider and the horizons run long.
hero.imageAlt: Extended family walking hand in hand across a golden field.

sections.heading: The Most Underrated Light in the Tri-Cities
paragraphs: I'll say something here I don't say on the other city pages: Pasco has light that people overlook.

Open sky and long horizons give the evening light room to stretch across the frame. Around open land, fewer visual interruptions let the sun stay low and warm, creating a spacious look that feels different from a busier streetscape.
I'm Lisa Weiss, based in Richland and photographing across the Tri-Cities since 2005. Pasco is part of my home coverage area, with no travel fee anywhere in Richland, Kennewick or Pasco.

Most outdoor family and senior sessions happen at golden hour, at a setting we choose together. Newborn sessions take place in your Pasco home. Branding sessions can happen at your business or on location, while professional headshots use portable studio lighting at your workplace. Planning and direction are part of every session.

sections.heading: Where Two Rivers Meet
paragraphs: The Snake and Columbia meet in Pasco, opening the landscape to water, driftwood, big sky and long views. For portraits, that combination gives us reflected light, room to move and a setting that can feel open without becoming empty.

I keep exact meeting points private, but I don't keep the planning mysterious. We choose the kind of setting together, and I set the time around the light. The specific place matters less than arriving when that light is ready. My guide explains more about how I choose locations across the Tri-Cities.

sections.heading: Farmland, Rows and Long Horizons
paragraphs: The agricultural landscape around Pasco changes through the year: blossoms in spring, deep green through summer and dusty gold as the season turns. Those shifts give the same wide horizon a different mood from one month to the next.

Rows do something specific in a photograph — they carry your eye straight through the frame and land it on the people. For senior pictures, open roads and long horizons create room to walk, turn and move without a crowded background.

For families, open space lets children move and interact instead of holding a pose. I choose the setting around the people first, then use the landscape to support the photograph rather than compete with it.

sections.heading: Seasons in Pasco
paragraphs: May through October is peak season across the Tri-Cities, and Pasco's open landscape is especially warm in late summer as fields turn gold. Fall dates fill first, so October sessions are best requested in late summer.
March and April bring blossoms, fresh green and milder evenings, with more room on the calendar. Spring can be a strong choice for families or seniors who want color without the pace of fall.

I also photograph year-round. A clear winter afternoon over open land can produce crisp, low light and a quieter palette. The season changes the look; it does not decide whether a meaningful session can happen.

items.heading: Do you travel to Pasco?
paragraphs: Yes. Richland, Kennewick and Pasco are all part of my home coverage area, with no travel fee anywhere in the Tri-Cities.

items.heading: What kinds of locations work well in Pasco?
paragraphs: Open country, farmland and river settings all work well. The right choice depends on the people, the season and the look you want, and I confirm the exact meeting point during planning.

items.heading: Where do newborn, branding and headshot sessions happen?
paragraphs: Newborn sessions happen in your Pasco home. Branding photography can happen at your business or on location, and I bring portable studio lighting to your workplace for professional headshots.

items.heading: When should I book?
paragraphs: Most sessions are reserved four to six weeks ahead. May through October is busiest and fall dates go first, so reach out in late summer if you are picturing October light.

finalCta.heading: Let's Find Your Light
paragraphs: Big sky, long horizons, and an evening that knows what it's doing. Tell me who you are bringing and what you want the photographs to feel like; I'll help plan the setting, timing and next steps.
